page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-focused instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 12 dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and runs on the KVM hypervisor. A defining characteristic of this instance is its bundled local storage, consisting of 35,433 GB of HDD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 1102.49 and single-threaded gzip compression rated as poor at 18.96 GB/sec. However, multi-core scaling is moderate, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 8789.97 and a PassMark CPU score of 10074.03, both falling in the average range. Memory bandwidth is stable, with read-only large block transfers reaching 54.9 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 47.08 GB/sec. PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations also perform within average parameters, achieving 8.27 million operations per second for Redis.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.d1.3xlarge offers high storage density per resource unit due to its massive HDD capacity. However, the reliance on traditional HDD storage instead of NVMe SSDs represents a significant tradeoff, limiting sequential and random I/O speeds compared to modern solid-state alternatives. Additionally, the weak single-core performance and lower memory score of 1685.71 on PassMark suggest that workloads requiring high-speed single-threaded processing or rapid memory access may experience bottlenecks.

This instance is suited for workloads that require massive, cost-effective storage capacity alongside moderate compute capabilities. Appropriate use cases include large-scale data archiving, cold storage, distributed file systems, and batch processing of large datasets where high-speed storage I/O is not a primary requirement. It is also applicable for hosting secondary database replicas or backup servers.
